audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart says Darius owns Level 6, first item and two-plus items. Every other field on the page says the opposite: whys[4] 'At 6 Maximum Dosage heals through your 5-stack execute for Mundo', whys[5] 'First item his HP and regen outrun your bleed DPS', whys[6] 'With two-plus items his ult and max-health cleaver make him unkillable', plus spikes[1..3], mid and late. The win rate says the same thing. Also carryRating and report[14].t say 8.5/10 while breakdown.carry says 7.5/10.
audit.why: Darius wins this only 47.59% over 3852 games - one of the worst numbers on his page - and the packet levelChart independently records Dr. Mundo at Level 6, first item and two-plus items. No drmundo__darius mirror file exists, so nothing on the other side pins these rows. Three separate sources agree against the chart and nothing agrees with it, so the chart is what is wrong. I am proposing the three flips as one atomic group with their ratings; I deliberately did NOT flip Level 3, where the evidence is thinner, and instead made whys[2] agree with the Skill verdict already recorded there.
audit.corrected: Level 6, first item and two-plus items all belong to Dr. Mundo.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 phase why is boilerplate about Noxian Guillotine and carries an un-rendered formula, 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. It never mentions Maximum Dosage, which is the only reason the stage moves. spikes[1].text then states that 'Your Guillotine can still reset on minions', which is not a thing the ability can do.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120 seconds and 'instantly healing a percent of his missing Health', then adds Move Speed and regeneration over a long duration. Because the heal scales off missing health, it returns more the closer you get him to dead - it is strongest at exactly the moment your execute becomes available. Noxian Guillotine 'leaps to an enemy champion' and refreshes only 'if Noxian Guillotine is a killing blow', so it cannot be cast on a minion and cannot reset off one. Grievous Wounds therefore has to be on him before he ults, not bought in reaction to it.
audit.corrected: Maximum Dosage is 120s and instantly heals a percent of his missing health, so it pays out most when you have him lowest.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two hard factual errors and one large omission. (a) The page calls Infected Bonesaw 'max-health' damage in whys[6] and spikes[2].text. Riot's text says current health. (b) Heart Zapper is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in eleven fields and its actual mechanic is never stated once - the page describes it only as a 'sustain spike + reset', and dontsFull[1].t calls it a 'W-reset', which is Blunt Force Trauma's property, not Heart Zapper's. (c) Blunt Force Trauma's missing-health scaling is nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw (Q, 4s, 975 range) deals 'damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health' - current, not max, so it hits hardest while you are healthy and tapers as the fight goes on, which is the opposite of the instinct the page teaches. Heart Zapper (W, 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s, 325 range) 'stor[es] a portion of damage he takes. At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage.' The heal is conditional on the burst connecting, so stepping outside 325 units before it pops denies the entire heal - that is the single most actionable fact in this matchup and it appears nowhere. Blunt Force Trauma (E, 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6s) deals 'additional damage based on his missing Health' and is an auto-attack reset, so a low Mundo is more dangerous than a healthy one, not less.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper only heals him if its end-of-duration burst hits someone - leave the 325-unit radius before it pops. Infected Bonesaw scales off your current health. Blunt Force Trauma hits harder the lower he is.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. breakdown.cooldowns is the field that should carry it and instead gives no numbers at all, then runs into two paragraphs of leaked source prose about Apprehend and Ghost.
audit.why: Heart Zapper 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, Maximum Dosage a flat 120, Infected Bonesaw 4, Blunt Force Trauma 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6, against Apprehend at 26/23.5/21/18.5/16. Heart Zapper's 17 seconds is the only window in the lane long enough to plan a commit around.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper 17s at rank 1 is the window; Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s.

audit.why: dosFull[0].t already says 'Rush a Grievous Wounds item', which is right and matches champ-data/_kits/_missing/darius.json flagging Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage as the anti-heal targets here. What was missing was the timing: because Maximum Dosage heals off missing health, the anti-heal has to be applied before he casts it, which I put into phases[4].why and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why ends in the orphan word 'Mundo.' and phases[2].why ends 'Mundo has to walk into pull range' with the opening clause missing. Both look like a find-and-replace that ate the surrounding text. breakdown.wave and report[4].t also carry the same leaked source block seen on camille and chogath, including the headings 'Key Mechanical Cooldowns' and 'How Darius Wins Trades' mid-paragraph.
audit.why: 'Access to Crippling Strike (W) auto-attack reset provides immense localized burst punishes. Mundo.' is not a sentence, and it is the level-2 advice on a page for a lane that is decided early.
audit.corrected: Rewritten so both phases read as complete advice.

notes: DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE - this is the biggest open question on the page. Six fields state that Goes Where He Pleases blocks or 'cleanses' Apprehend: tldr ('Pop spellshield canister with E'), breakdown.early, spikes[3].text ('passive cleanses one disable every few seconds (dodging your E pull)'), the mid text, the late text, and whys[2]. Riot's text says the passive 'resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him', while Apprehend 'sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him' - a displacement, which is not obviously an immobilizing effect. Whether a pull triggers the passive is exactly the class of thing champ-data marks unknown, and the kit file compounds it by tagging Darius's E with a 'knockup' flag his description does not support. I rewrote whys[2] and the tldr around facts I could source rather than repeating the claim, and left the other four fields untouched. If the passive does not eat Apprehend, four fields are telling the player his engage is countered when it is not, and that changes how the whole lane is played. Note also that the passive's cooldown is null in the kit, so 'every few seconds' in spikes[3].text has no source. Separately: breakdown.wave and report[4].t carry the same leaked source block found on camille and chogath.
